html:
Rajaraja I was the Chola king who ruled from Thanjavur in south India from 985 to 1014 and turned a regional kingdom into a sea power.

His wars went in every direction:

  • South, he beat the Pandyas and the Cheras of Kerala.
  • Across the strait, he took northern Sri Lanka, sacked Anuradhapura and ruled from Polonnaruwa.
  • North, he fought the Western Chalukyas and tied the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi to his family by marriage.
  • At sea, his fleet took islands that included the Maldives.

At home he had land surveyed for tax and kept careful records in stone. His greatest monument is the Brihadisvara Temple in Thanjavur, finished in 1010, whose walls list his gifts and its staff.

His son Rajendra I went further still, marching to the Ganges and sending the raid on Srivijaya in 1025.
sum: Rajaraja I was the Chola king who ruled from Thanjavur in south India from 985 to 1014 and turned a regional kingdom into a sea power.
